Data sources, licences and limitations

Data sources, licences and limitations

UNDP · Tajikistan–Kyrgyzstan borderlands. Mapping by Hugh Lamarque. Prepared from the supplied QGIS package, 28 October 2026.

Study area

The study includes Sughd Region, Batken region, Nookat district and Osh city. A 5 km buffer on each side of the Osh–Nookat road connects Nookat to the municipality, restricted to their combined bounding envelope and Kyrgyzstan. Only the intersecting parts of Aravan and Kara-Suu are included. Osh city and the approach contribute to all study totals. Sughd is retained for the Tajikistan country office. The programme summary supports links through Osh, Batken, Isfara and Sughd; the ToR focuses on Batken–Kyzyl-Bel–Isfara. The exact extent and approach width are analytical choices, not a programme-prescribed beneficiary boundary. Analytical administrative polygons predate the 2025 agreement; neither they nor the OSM display reference have been verified against its implementation.

Data coverage · GeoJSON · Programme working extent · GeoJSON · Geographic selection · JSON

National borders use one OpenStreetMap reference network, deduplicated by shared boundary-way IDs from the 27 October 2026 extracts. This avoids stacking disagreeing country outlines. The dashed green line marks the working study extent; it is not a national border. Enclave borders remain visible. Continuous data coverage includes enclosed territories, with their source-country attribution retained. Whole-coverage totals include those territories; inclusion does not establish programme eligibility. Names and boundaries do not imply United Nations endorsement or acceptance; this reference has not been verified against the 2025 agreement.

ThemeSource and dateInterpretation
National borders and administrative areasNational reference: OSM · 27 October 2026 · ODbL. Analytical polygons: supplied HDX/OCHA and geoBoundaries files.Shared OSM boundary ways are drawn once. The separate study outline and analytical polygons are not treaty-validated boundaries.
Roads, places, services and infrastructureOpenStreetMap extracts · 27 October 2026 · © OpenStreetMap contributors · ODbL.Coverage varies. Named towns are OSM nodes, not census footprints. Calculated road–boundary intersections are not verified open border posts.
PopulationWorldPop 2025 R2025A · constrained, UN-adjusted · 1 km counts.Exact equal-area pixel overlap allocates source counts. Hex values are people/km². Missing source cells remain unknown; they do not establish an absence of population.
Population near roadsWorldPop 2025 and OSM 27 October 2026.Dissolved 10 km buffers on either side of motorway, trunk, primary roads and links. Country rows use that country’s roads. Straight-line proximity, not travel time or operational accessibility.
Local connectivityOriginal shared OSM node IDs and a directed local-road graph.Paths up to 10 km on non-major roads, one-way and motor-access tags, 250 m settlement snap, 20 km halo. Raw nodes are not merged interchanges. No turn restrictions, live closures or border-operability model.
Built-up surfaceJRC GHSL R2023A · 2000, 2018 and 2020 · European Commission reuse terms.2018 native 10 m values averaged to 100 m; 2000/2020 use native 100 m surface. Land share, not occupied buildings or population. Changes may include model differences.
Night-time lightsEOG VIIRS monthly radiance · August 2026.Mean valid radiance (nW/cm²/sr) per hex; an indirect activity indicator affected by background noise and coverage. Uneven display bands emphasise lower radiance without changing source values.
Land coverESA WorldCover 2021, 10 m · CC BY 4.0.Systematic approximately 100 m sample of source classes; proportions are sampled, not full-resolution area accounting.
Relative deprivationGRDI v1.10 · 2025 release.Composite relative index, 0–100; not a poverty percentage. Valid-area-weighted summaries exclude source gaps and are not population weighted.
River floodWRI Aqueduct Floods · historical 25-year return-period inundation.Mean valid depth per hex; not a current forecast or annual flood probability.
Recorded eventsACLED extract through 28 October 2025; study records 7 January 2018–15 October 2025. ACLED terms apply.No 2026 coverage. All supplied event types, including protests and riots. Reporting and location precision vary; fatalities are reported estimates.
Satellite basemapEsri World Imagery and its contributors.Imagery dates and resolution vary. Provider terms and attribution apply.
RainfallCHIRPS v3 · annual 2025 and September 2026 · 0.05°.Area-weighted rainfall totals in mm. Not anomalies or drought severity. Valid source-cell intersections; no population weighting. Source clips and provenance are downloadable in Analysis.
Healthcare travel timeMalaria Atlas Project · nominal 2019, published 2020 · approximately 1 km. WorldPop 2025 counts.Native-grid provider clips. Exact source-cell overlap allocates population to 5 km cells and analysis areas; 30 / 60 / 120-minute bands are available. Historical model, not current border permission or facility operation. Friction clips are routing inputs.
Surface waterJRC Global Surface Water v1.5 · occurrence 1984–2024; seasonality 2024.Original approximately 30 m cells weighted by area and assigned by centre. Zero is valid; missing observations are excluded. Detection frequency differs from water-area share. Display images are reduced-resolution overviews.
Urban centresJRC GHS-UCDB R2024A v1.2 · 2025 epoch.Ten source centroids inside the study. Whole original footprints and modelled populations are retained, including portions outside the study. Not municipal boundaries or census counts; smaller towns may be absent.

Corrected full QGIS refresh builder · Python · v2.0.1 recognises MAP .geotiff archive members. Scanner repair tested; no rerun is needed for the healthcare layers now on this site.

Inputs still needed

Country-office-verified programme sites, dated crossing and facility operations, rural road access, rainfall anomalies, longer surface-water time series, groundwater, water-point surveys and historical humid heat remain to be added. Unsupported controls are marked unavailable. Healthcare, surface-water summaries and urban centres are now available alongside rainfall totals and IATI records.

Interpretation

Map and Analysis share the same study area and data. Five-kilometre hexagons are clipped analytical units, measured flat-to-flat (about 21.65 km² for a full cell). Smaller cells do not increase source resolution. Continuous data coverage includes enclosed territories; source NoData remains missing. Source dates describe the inputs, not current operating conditions.
